findings.title: Document AI service agent is never granted access to the CMEK key it's configured to use
findings.explanation: google_document_ai_processor.main now sets kms_key_name (correctly, per provider 7.31.0 docs), and the example wires in a real key via google_kms_crypto_key.docai. But per Google's own Document AI CMEK documentation, the Document AI Service Agent (service-<PROJECT_NUMBER>@gcp-sa-prod-dai-core.iam.gserviceaccount.com) must separately hold roles/cloudkms.cryptoKeyEncrypterDecrypter on that key before CMEK will work — Terraform never grants this automatically, and no google_kms_crypto_key_iam_member/binding exists anywhere in this repo. HLD_GCP_242 (CMEK required) and HLD_GCP_107 (referenced key must have rotation enabled) both pass because they only check attributes on the two resources in isolation; neither can see that the *access grant* linking them is missing. Without it, `terraform apply` on the example fails at processor-creation time with a permission-denied error. This is the exact same gap the workspace's own terraform-gcp-filestore module encodes as a custom policy (HLD_GCP_474) and terraform-gcp-pubsub already fixes with a dedicated google_kms_crypto_key_iam_member + google_project_service_identity pair — this module is the outlier that's missing it.

findings.title: CMEK key ring is located in the "eu" multi-region, but Document AI requires the key in "europe-west4" for eu-multi-region processors
findings.explanation: The example sets both the processor's location and the KMS key ring's location to "eu" on the assumption they must match. Google's Document AI CMEK documentation states the location of the key must match the processor's location *except* for the "us" and "eu" multi-regions, where the key must instead be in "us-central1" and "europe-west4" respectively — "eu" is not a valid Cloud KMS location for a key backing an eu-multi-region Document AI processor's CMEK. No deterministic rule can catch this: it requires knowing Document AI's specific location-mapping exception, not a generic same-location comparison. As configured, applying the example would create the key fine (eu is a valid KMS multi-region) but Document AI would reject the CMEK linkage at processor-creation time.
findings.remediation: Change example/examplea/google_kms_key_ring.tf location from "eu" to "europe-west4" (google_kms_crypto_key.docai inherits location from the key ring, so only the key ring needs updating). Leave var.location = "eu" on the processor/module itself unchanged — only the key's location is wrong.
findings.fix:
In example/examplea/google_kms_key_ring.tf, change:
  location = "eu"
to:
  location = "europe-west4"

suggested_policies.rationale: Setting kms_key_name on google_document_ai_processor does not by itself grant the Document AI service agent permission to use the key — GCP requires a separate IAM grant (roles/cloudkms.cryptoKeyEncrypterDecrypter to the service agent) that Terraform never creates automatically. This is structurally identical to the workspace's own HLD_GCP_474 (filestore) policy, just for a different resource type; coverage_by_type.google_document_ai_processor only lists HLD_GCP_242 (CMEK required), nothing checks the access grant. The condition is a plain requires_companion linked via kms_key_name -> crypto_key_id, so it fits the existing DSL with no extension.
suggested_policies.yaml:
id: HLD_PROPOSED_001
name: Document AI processors using CMEK must grant the Document AI service agent key access
principle: key-management
severity: HIGH
rationale: |
  Setting kms_key_name on a google_document_ai_processor does not by itself
  grant Document AI's service agent permission to use the key. GCP requires
  the Document AI Service Agent
  (service-<PROJECT_NUMBER>@gcp-sa-prod-dai-core.iam.gserviceaccount.com) to
  hold roles/cloudkms.cryptoKeyEncrypterDecrypter on the referenced key, via
  a separate IAM binding that Terraform never creates automatically. Without
  it, processor creation fails at apply time with a permission-denied error.
remediation: |
  Grant the Document AI service agent access to the key:

    resource "google_project_service_identity" "documentai" {
      provider = google-beta
      service  = "documentai.googleapis.com"
    }

    resource "google_kms_crypto_key_iam_member" "documentai" {
      crypto_key_id = google_kms_crypto_key.main.id
      role          = "roles/cloudkms.cryptoKeyEncrypterDecrypter"
      member        = "serviceAccount:${google_project_service_identity.documentai.email}"
    }
resources:
  google_document_ai_processor:
    filter:
      path: kms_key_name
      not_null: true
    any:
      - requires_companion:
          type: google_kms_crypto_key_iam_member
          linked_via:
            from: kms_key_name
            to: crypto_key_id
          where:
            path: role
            equals: roles/cloudkms.cryptoKeyEncrypterDecrypter
      - requires_companion:
          type: google_kms_crypto_key_iam_binding
          linked_via:
            from: kms_key_name
            to: crypto_key_id
          where:
            path: role
            equals: roles/cloudkms.cryptoKeyEncrypterDecrypter

suggested_policies.rationale: Document AI enforces an undocumented-to-Terraform location-matching rule between a CMEK key and its processor: locations must match exactly, except the 'us' and 'eu' multi-regions, which require the key in 'us-central1' / 'europe-west4' specifically. This is broadly applicable to any google_document_ai_processor + google_kms_crypto_key pairing, not just this repo, but the current DSL's linked_resource/requires_companion primitives only support direct attribute equality between linked resources — they can't express 'equal, except when source is one of these special values, in which case it must equal this other specific value instead'.
suggested_policies.yaml:
id: HLD_PROPOSED_002
name: Document AI CMEK key location must match processor location (with us/eu multi-region exceptions)
principle: key-management
severity: HIGH
rationale: |
  The location of a Document AI processor's CMEK key must match the
  processor's location, except for the 'us' and 'eu' multi-regions, where
  the key must instead be located in 'us-central1' and 'europe-west4'
  respectively. A key in the wrong location causes the CMEK linkage to be
  rejected at processor-creation time even though both resources apply
  independently without error.
remediation: |
  Set the KMS key ring's location to match the processor's location, using
  'us-central1' if the processor location is 'us', 'europe-west4' if it is
  'eu', or the same value otherwise.
resources:
  google_document_ai_processor:
    filter:
      path: kms_key_name
      not_null: true
    any:
      - linked_resource:
          type: google_kms_crypto_key
          via: kms_key_name
          to: id
          must:
            path: location
            location_equivalent_map:
              source_path: location
              mapping:
                us: us-central1
                eu: europe-west4
              default: match_source
suggested_policies.dsl_extension_note: Needs a new cross-resource comparison operator (working name: location_equivalent_map) usable inside a linked_resource.must block. Semantics: read the source resource's attribute at source_path (here, google_document_ai_processor.location); if its value is a key in mapping, the target attribute (google_kms_crypto_key.location) must equal the mapped value; otherwise (default: match_source) the target attribute must equal the source value exactly. This generalizes beyond Document AI to any GCP service with multi-region-to-specific-region CMEK key mapping quirks (several Google services follow the same us/eu multi-region convention).
